questions.question:
**Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence.**

She did not forget me even though I have been away for a year.

options.text: I was not forgotten by her even though I have been away for a year.
Even though I have been away for a year she had not been forgotten.
Even though I have been away for a year she did not forget me.
Though I have been away for a year she has not forgot me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**I was not forgotten by her even though I have been away for a year.'**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **assertive** sentence.
 
• We need to follow these instructions while changing the voice of an assertive sentence.
 
 
• Find the subject and object of the sentence and exchange their places; make changes in their cases as well if subject and object are pronouns.
 
• In the given sentence the subject is '**s****he**,' while the object is ‘**I**’.
 
• Use preposition **'by' **before agent '**she'.**
 
 

Following these steps, we finally get - "I was not forgotten by her even though I have been away for a year."

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Most lizards rely on camouflage to hide from their enemies.

options.text: Camouflage has been relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.
Camouflage is relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.
Camouflage was relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.
Most lizards are being relied on by camouflage to hide from their enemies.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Camouflage is relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the passive voice, the *subject__ is __acted upon__ by the __verb__.*

 __
 
• Example: Kho-kho is liked by Upasana.
 
 
 
• In the active voice, the *subject__ __performs__ an __action__.*
 
 
• Example: Upasana likes kho-kho.
 
 
 
• The formula used for a present active voice is:
 
 
• Subject (Most lizards) + V1 (rely on) + Object (Camouflage) + Remaining Sentence (if any).
 
 
 
• So, we know that the sentence is in the present active voice so for changing the present active voice into the present passive voice. The formula used will be :
 
 
• Object (Camouflage) + is/am/are + V3 (relied on) + by + Subject (most lizards) + Remaining Sentence (if any).
 
 

Hence, **option 2) Camouflage is relied on by most lizards to hide from their enemies **is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Someone stole his traveller's cheques when he was travelling in Europe.

options.text: His traveller's cheques was stole when he was travelling in Europe.
Someone had been stole his traveller's cheques when he was travelling in Europe.
His traveller's cheques were stolen when he was travelling in Europe.
His traveller's cheques are stole when he was travelling in Europe.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'His traveller's cheques were stolen when he was travelling in Europe.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The following rules should be kept in mind while converting **active into passive voice:**

 
 
• The **subject** in the** active voice** becomes the **object** in the **passive voice **and the **object in the active voice** becomes the **subject in the passive voice.**
 
• Put ‘**by**’ in front of the **subject** in the **passive voice.**
 
• **is/ am/ are/ was/ were/ being + Use 3rd form of the verb **according to the **tense** in** the passive voice.**
 
 
 
• **​**Therefore, keeping in mind all these rules, we can conclude that **option 3 **is the **correct answer**.

 

**The correct sentence is:**__ *'His traveller's cheques were stolen when he was travelling in Europe.'*

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the option that is the passive form of the given sentence.**

The police brought a search warrant when they raided his house.

options.text: A search warrant had been brought when the police raided his house.
The police had raided his house and brought a search warrant.
A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.
A search warrant was brought when they raided his house by the police.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **According to the rule of grammar,** the subject of the sentence is 'the police' and the object of the sentence is 'a search warrant' hence the rule says that in the passive voice the subject of the sentence becomes the object and the object of the sentence becomes the subject.
 
• *The main verb of the sentence is 'Brought' which tells that it is in the past tense hence in the passive voice the tense will not be changed.*
 
• *Also, the sequence of the clauses should not be changed too. 'When they raided his house' should be at the end position.*

**So the correct sentence is-** *A search warrant was brought by the police when they raided his house.* i.e.* *option 3.* *

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.**

Imran has found two good jobs in the advertisements of the newspaper.

options.text: Two good jobs are being found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.
Two good jobs had found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.
Two good jobs have been found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.
Two good jobs has found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option 3) i.e., 'Two good jobs have been found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The given sentence is an **assertive sentence**. 
 
• We need to follow these instructions while **changing the voice of an assertive sentence.**
 
 
• Find the **subject and object **of the sentence and **exchange their places**.
 
• In the given sentence the **subject is ‘Imran’**, while the **object is ‘two good jobs**’.
 
• Use **preposition by **before agent. (Imran)
 
• Always use **the third form (have been found) **of the **main verb (has found)** in passive form. 
 
• At last line up the remaining part. 
 
 
 
• Following these steps, we finally get - " **Two good jobs have been found by Imran in the advertisements of the newspaper.**"
 
• Hence, **option 3 **is the correct answer.

__
 
• The given sentence is interrogative and in **Present Perfect Tense,**** Active Voice**.
 
• The rule for changing a Present Perfect Tense, Active Voice from Active voice to Passive voice:
 
 
• Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• Structure: Why + do + Subject + have + to + V1 + Object​ (Active Voice)__ 
 
 

 Why + do + Object + have to be + V3 + by Subject​ __(Passive Voice)__

__
 
• Example: *Why do we have to do the tasks?** *(Active Voice)

 * * *Why do the tasks have to be done by us? *(Passive Voice)​

 
• Therefore, the correct answer is 'Why do the house chores have to be done by us during this lockdown period?'

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, the sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
 
• Example: *He reads a novel. *(Active Voice)*​*
 
• *A novel is read by him. *(Passive Voice)

questions.question:
**Select the correct passive voice of the given sentence.**

You must repeat your main points (not the sub-points).

options.text: Your main points (not the sub-points) must be repeated by you.
The main points (not the sub-points) can be repeated by you.
The main points (not the sub-points) are repeated by you.
You must be repeated your main points (not the sub-points).

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Your main points (not the sub-points) must be repeated by you.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• The given sentence is in the active form and **imperative sentence** and we need to change it into the passive form.
 
• The Imperative sentence in the active voice has the following form: Subject + modal + infinitive + object__
 
• The Imperative sentence in the passive voice has the following form: __Object + modal + be + past participle + by Subject__
 
• In the passive voice of the imperative sentence, we have to change the structure, so the subject in the passive voice becomes the object in the active voice.

​Therefore, the correct answer is option 1.

__Correct Active Voice:__ *Your main points (not the sub-points) must be repeated by you.*
